<reason>Both sides executed the format cleanly and landed sharp exchanges, but PRO held the decisive weighing. CON's two best lines — that PRO's enforcement signals depend on the legal research ecosystem, and that the definitional line rests on knowledge the ban forbids generating — were answered squarely: PRO redefined enforcement as human signals (whistleblowers, criminalized assistance, blocked funding/journals, stripped camouflage) and redefined the line as prospective intent-based (engineering transmissibility plus escape), which blunts the epistemic regress. Meanwhile PRO's pressure on payoff forced a real concession (no deployed vaccine required creating a novel pandemic virus), which PRO leveraged into the "certain existence versus speculative insight" weighing that CON never fully dismantled. CON's claim that prohibition dissolves the oversight chokepoints was overstated, since PRO repeatedly noted that sequencing, platforms, and most virology remain legal. PRO's closing crystallized the choice more decisively.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>The B3.2 pressure question ("name one deployed defense that required first creating a novel pandemic virus") forced CON's concession in A4.3, and PRO converted it in B4.5 and B5.4 into the debate's central weighing: certain existence of a lab-made threat versus speculative defensive insight.</best_rebuttal>
